questions.q:
Given below are two statements, one is labelled as& Assertion $A$~and the other is labelled as~Reason $R .$

Assertion A:~The spin only magnetic moment value for \left[Fe ( CN{)}_{6}\right]3 -$~is $1 . 74BM,$ whereas for~[Fe(H2O)6]\left[Fe\left({H}_{2}O\right)6\right]3 +$ is~$5 . 92BM .$

Reason B:~In both complexes, $Fe$ is present in $+ 3$ oxidation state.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both& $A$~and~$R$~are true but~$R$~is~$NOT$~the correct explanation of~$A$
Both $A$ and $R$ are true and$R$ is the correct explanation of~$A$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
$[ Fe ( {H}_{2}O{)}_{6}{]}^{3 +}$~has~magnetic moment value of $5 . 92BM$~because~${H}_{2}O$ is a~weak ligand and pairing will not occur. It~involves~${sp}^{3}d^{2}$ hybridisation with five unpaired electrons (because magnetic moment is equal to $5 . 92BM$) and outer~orbital complex is formed.~Magnetic moment can be calculated by the formula~${μ}_{m} = \sqrt{n ( n + 2 )}$~$BM$~where,~${μ}_{m} =$magnetic moment,~$n =$number of unpaired electron(s).

${μ}_{m} = 1 . 74BM, n = 1{μ}_{m} = 5 . 92BM, n = 5$

In~$[ Fe ( CN{)}_{6}{]}^{3 –}$complex~${CN}^{−}$~is stronger ligand than ${H}_{2}O$ according to spectrochemical series. ~Hence, four~electrons will pair itself. It~involves $d^{2}{sp}^{3}$hybridisation with one unpaired electron and inner orbital complex is formed and has a value of only~$1 . 74BM$.

In Bothe the complexes the oxidation state of iron is +3.

Outer orbital Complex, Inner orbital Complex

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
In the complex \left[Co\left({NH}_{3}\right)6\right]3 +$ Ammonia is strong field ligand and electronic configuration of

${Co}^{3 +}⇒ 3d^{6} \left({t}_{2g}^{6}, {e}_g^{0}\right)

Hybridisation: $d^{2}{sp}^{3}$

Pairing of electrons takes place due to the strong field ligand. Hence, it is inner orbital complex (spin paired complex).

In the complex \left[{CoF}_{6}\right]3 -$ fluoride is weak field ligand and electronic configuration of ${Co}^{3 +}⇒ 3d^{6} \left({t}_{2g}^{4}, {e}_g^{2}\right).

Hybridisation: ${sp}^{3}d^{2}$

Pairing of electrons not takes place due to the weak field ligand. Hence, it is outer orbital complex (spin free complex).

Hence option B is the answer.

questions.q: Which of the following cannot be explained by crystal field theory?
options: Magnetic properties of transition metal complexes
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution: The crystal field model is successful in explaining the formation, structures, colour and magnetic properties of coordination compounds to a large extent. However, from the assumptions that the ligands are point charges, it follows that anionic ligands should exert the greatest splitting effect. The anionic ligands actually are found at the low end of the spectrochemical series. So, it couldn't explain successfully the order of spectrochemical series.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The number of unpaired electrons in coordination complexes is determined by the nature of the central metal ion, the coordination number, and the identity and arrangement of the ligands around the metal ion. Based on these factors, the correct order of the number of unpaired electrons in the given complexes is:

A \left[Fe ( CN{)}_{6}\right]3 -: {Fe}^{3 +}\left(3d^{5}\right)$~(Pairing of electrons takes place) $1$

C \left[{CoF}_{6}\right]3 -: {Co}^{3 +} \left($3d^{6}\right)$ $4$
D \left[Cr ( oxalate{)}_{3}\right]3 -: {Cr}^{3 +}\left(3d^{3}\right)$ $3$
E \left[$Ni ( CO{)}_{4}\right]: Ni \left(3d^{10}\right)$(Pairing of electrons takes place) $0$

No. of unpaired electrons order:~$E < A < D < C < B$

$
